newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's trade trend improves in August - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ's trade trend improves in August - SNZ.

text.p: New Zealand's trade balance on a smoothed trend estimate continued to improve in August, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday. .
This was due to the exports trend increasing by 1.2 percent per month on average since February against the imports trend averaging 0.3 percent growth per month over the same period.
In August, the unadjusted deficit was $384.8 million, up $132 million on August 1995. Excluding large one-off items (the import of an oil tanker), the deficit would have been $280 million.
In August, the unadjusted value of exports was $1.65 billion, down by 2.7 percent on August 1995.
Major contributors to the decrease were fish, down $23 million, ships and boats, down $18 million and unwrought aluminium, down $15 million.
Imports in August were up by 4.4 percent on the same month last year to $2.04 billion.
Exports in the August quarter were up 1.0 percent over the 1995 quarter at $5.16 billion. Over the same period imports rose by 4.7 percent to $5.62 billion.
The deficit for the quarter of $464 million was $200 million greater than in the August 1995 quarter.
In the August year, exports fell 0.6 percent to $20.91 billion while imports rose by 0.5 percent to $21.59 billion. The deficit of $676 million compared with $453 million in the August 1995 year.
